newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers differ on compulsory beef labelling.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers differ on compulsory beef labelling.

text.p: European Union farm ministers on Monday gave conflicting views on a proposal to try and restore consumer confidence in beef after the mad cow disease health scare by making it compulsory to state the origin of the beef.

"I am in favour, very much in favour," French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur told Reuters before the meeting, adding he hoped that agreement on compulsory labelling from January 2000 would rapidly be reached.
But the European Commission's proposal would also give the European Parliament an equal say in the decision -- something which France opposes.
Belgian Farm Minister Karel Pinxten, who supported compulsory labelling, said the European Parliament must play a role but he was unsure if it should be joint decision-making.

Portuguese Farm Minister Fernando Gomes da Silva, another supporter of compulsory labelling, said the proposal must be changed but it would need unanimous agreement among the 15 member states to overrule the Commission.
Danish Farm Minister Henrik Dam Kristensen said he was did not think agreement would be reached.
"I'm a little bit pessimistic," he told reporters before the meeting. "I think the proposal is too bureaucratic."
British officials said Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg would ask for more time to study the revised proposal, presented earlier this month, as there were points he did not like.
Britain believes that the proposal would stir nationalist sentiment and create a barrier to trade in the EU single market.
